normie.tagline: Guess how good everyday detectors are.
normie.quip: Sniffer dogs, lie detectors, smoke alarms. Every one of them lies sometimes.
normie.helpQuip: No detector is perfect. Some are hilariously far from it.
help: Each day brings one real detector, from smoke alarms and sniffer dogs to lie detectors and AI checkers. Normie mode: no medicine.
Slide two bars: when the thing is really there, how often does it catch it? When it isn’t, how often does it stay quiet?
Closer guesses score more, up to 100 a round. Where studies disagree, anywhere in the range scores full marks.
The reveal shows 100 cases: catches, misses and false alarms, with the source.
Some rounds have a bonus twist: the alarm goes off, so what’s the chance it’s for real?

sensitosis: Sensitosis in Normie mode is a daily guessing game about how good everyday detectors are. Each day brings one real one, from smoke alarms and sniffer dogs to lie detectors, facial recognition and AI-writing checkers. Slide two bars to guess how often each one catches the real thing and how often it stays quiet when there’s nothing there. Then see 100 cases on a grid, with the real figure and its source.
No. Normie scores and streaks are kept separately.
What do ‘catches it’ and ‘stays quiet’ mean?

Catches it (sensitivity): out of 100 times the thing is really there, how many times the detector goes off. Stays quiet (specificity): out of 100 times it isn’t there, how many times it keeps quiet. The rest are false alarms.
Yes. Every figure comes from a published study or report, linked on every reveal and rounded. Studies vary, so treat them as ballpark.
